items.title: Randy Sandke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997
items.q: And the thing is, take for instance Ornette Coleman. And I have great respect for him... But for instance like “Harmolodic” is this term that every musician knows but nobody knows what it is.

ctx.x: The Harmolodic but I’m not sure I understand it.

Well see that’s the thing. See that’s something that again bothers me, and to me shows a deficiency of the jazz criticism and the fact that I mean like some of the jazz critics I have good relationships with, some I would even, one or two I would even consider kind of friends. But speaking in general terms they usually don’t have a serious musical © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

background, which that doesn’t invalidate all their opinions, but I think sometimes it puts them at a disadvantage. And the thing is, take for instance Ornette Coleman. And I have great respect for him, especially the stuff he did with Don Cherry, a lot of that stuff I think is great. And he really opened up things, and an incredibly important figure.
